---
title: "How do I compare the distribution of measurements across groups?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I compare the distribution of measurements across groups?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Match each numeric value to its group.

2. Count cases in each group with table().

3. Plot value

group and label the measurement units.

## Runnable example

```{r}
site <- rep(c("coast","inland"),each=6)
temp_c <- c(12,13,12,15,14,13,18,19,20,21,18,22)
print(table(site))
boxplot(temp_c ~ site,col=c("#CEE2F0","#EAC99E"),
        main="Temperatures by setting",ylab="Temperature (C)",xlab="Setting")
legend("topright",legend=c("Coast","Inland"),
       fill=c("#CEE2F0","#EAC99E"),bty="n")
```

## Interpret the result

The groups can be compared on one temperature scale. The graph describes these sample observations; it does not by itself establish a causal difference.

## Check before applying to real data

Check the sample sizes per group; visually different medians alone do not establish a statistically significant difference.
